title: Rabbi Netanel
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer, chapter 17](https://www.sefaria.org/Pirkei_DeRabbi_Eliezer.17), where he said: “Three hundred years before Josiah was born, his name was named.” In [chapter 25](https://www.sefaria.org/Pirkei_DeRabbi_Eliezer.25) he is mentioned after Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha. In [chapter 48](https://www.sefaria.org/Pirkei_DeRabbi_Eliezer.48) he said: “Moses’ parents saw that his appearance was like an angel’s; they circumcised him at eight days and named him Yekutiel.” Rabbi Shimon says: “They named him Tov.” From this we see that he lived in the time of the tannaim.[^1][^2]

notes.text: ד״ה א׳ and פדר״א are rendered by the customary titles I Chronicles and Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer. The parenthetical name reference is printed פ׳טו-כד, read conventionally as chapter 15, verse 24, not multiple verses. טוב is the name Tov, parallel to Yekutiel, rather than the adverb “well” in the earlier English. אמר attributes the saying to Netanel, not to the book as an unnamed speaker. The chapter numbers and Hyman’s inference about the tannaitic period are retained as his account; no named edition was checked in the earlier preparation; the subsequent bounded title comparison is noted below.

The Sefaria Vocalized Edition of Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer explicitly titles Netanel in chapters 17 and 25, Yehoshua ben Korcha in chapter 25, and Shimon in chapter 48. These support the retained expanded titles. That edition places Netanel before Yehoshua ben Korcha, whereas Hyman says after; its Moses naming paragraph begins with an unnamed ‘Rabbi.’ Hyman’s sequence and his attribution of the latter saying to Netanel remain his account, not a harmonization of the versions.
